question: A 9-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents with a 2-day history of weakness and joint pain. He was adopted 3 weeks ago from an international adoption agency and this is his first week in the United States. He says that he has been healthy and that he had an episode of sore throat shortly before his adoption. Physical exam reveals an ill-appearing boy with a fever, widespread flat red rash, and multiple subcutaneous nodules. The type of hypersensitivity seen in this patient's disease is also characteristic of which of the following diseases?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "International adoption" -> "Recent travel" -> "Possible exposure to infectious agents" -> "Increased risk of infectious diseases" -> 80% CHAIN: "Sore throat before adoption" -> "Possible history of infection" -> "Immune response triggered" -> "Development of hypersensitivity reaction" -> 85% CHAIN: "Ill-appearing boy with fever" -> "Systemic inflammatory response" -> "Immune system activation" -> "Hypersensitivity reaction" -> 90% CHAIN: "Widespread flat red rash" -> "Cutaneous manifestation of hypersensitivity" -> "Type IV hypersensitivity reaction" -> "Characteristic of serum sickness" -> 95% CHAIN: "Multiple subcutaneous nodules" -> "Subcutaneous granulomas" -> "Immune complex deposition" -> "Characteristic of serum sickness" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with fever, rash, joint pain, and subcutaneous nodules is suggestive of acute rheumatic fever, which is a complication of untreated streptococcal pharyngitis. The hypersensitivity seen in this disease is a type II hypersensitivity reaction, which is also characteristic of Goodpasture syndrome.
